transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-31
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sophie (Redwood CSM), Dr. Anna (Solstice Head of ML), Samir (Platform), Laura (Security), Tom (Product), Jorge (contractor)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on onboarding runway for Solstice Health's inference migration. Covered deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC), compliance needs (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), initial performance targets, and next steps: share security pack, schedule infra review, and get traffic profile.

Topics:
- Onboarding timeline and success criteria
- Network & data residency constraints
- Performance and cost targets (p99 latency, tokens/sec)
- Pilot plan (canary traffic, model pinning, rollbacks)
- Observability and runbooks

Action items recap (see metadata above).

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 40 minutes, so we'll run through a quick intake + kickoff. Ethan and Sophie are on from our side. Would you like to do quick intros?
[00:12] Dr. Anna Rivera (Solstice): Yeah hi, I'm Anna, I run ML at Solstice. We build clinical summarization and triage models for telehealth.
[00:18] Samir Gupta (Solstice): Samir, platform eng, responsible for infra and network.
[00:21] Laura Kim (Solstice): Laura, security and compliance.
[00:23] Tom Hale (Solstice): Tom on product. Jorge is helping with integration later.
[00:28] Maya: Great thanks. High level: Solstice wants to move inference for two critical flows—symptom triage and visit summarization—onto Redwood to reduce latency and ops burden while meeting your compliance reqs. Today? Anna: we still run a mix of hosted and self-hosted, a few models on prem.
[00:45] Dr. Anna: Yep, we have some models on an internal cluster (NVIDIA A100s), but it's brittle, maintenance heavy, and we hit spikes during clinic hours. We need predictable SLOs and easier rollouts.
[00:58] Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE): Thanks Anna. Quick question for the performance targets: what's your p50/p95/p99 latency target and typical QPS per flow? That will help us recommend Dedicated sizing and batching parameters.
[01:10] Dr. Anna: For triage the p95 should be < 150ms ideally, p99 < 400ms. QPS varies—baseline 10 qps, peak up to 120 qps during morning windows. Summarization is more tolerant: p95 < 700ms, peak maybe 30 qps.
[01:26] Ethan: Got it. Those targets will determine whether Hosted with autoscaling can hit p99 or if Dedicated pools are better. We often recommend Dedicated for consistent p99 at high peaks, or Hosted with burst plans if you want less ops overhead.
[01:40] Samir: Network constraints: our infra is in AWS us-west-2 and we require VPC peering or PrivateLink for any managed endpoint. Also we have strict egress controls, so any hosted option must support VPC endpoints.
[01:52] Maya: Understood. Our Redwood Private (VPC) product supports a customer-managed VPC with private control plane, and Hosted supports PrivateLink for enterprise accounts. We'll share the VPC connectivity doc.
[02:05] Laura: From compliance: SOC2 Type II required, SAML SSO for console access, RBAC scoped to teams, and KMS integration for key management. Also we need audit logs retained for 12 months.
[02:17] Sophie Martinez (CSM): We support SSO via SAML, RBAC, and can surface audit logs in the Console. Retention is an add-on but we can include a 12-month retention package in the proposal.
[02:29] Laura: Great, can you also confirm where tokens/embeddings data persists and encryption at rest specifics?
[02:35] Ethan: Yes, data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys in Private deployments. For Hosted, we use encrypted disks with provider-managed KMS by default but can integrate with customer KMS on Dedicated/Private. We'll include the KMS/HSM integration steps in the security pack.
[02:49] Tom: On the migration plan—we want a pilot with two models: triage (smaller context) and the summarizer (longer context). Would you recommend starting on Hosted then move to Dedicated if we see tail latency issues?
[03:02] Ethan: That's a common path—start Hosted to iterate faster and lower initial cost, then reserve Dedicated for predictable peaks. Alternatively, if the p99 requirement is firm and you prefer predictable cost, we can spin up a small Dedicated pool and use canary routing.
[03:15] Dr. Anna: We have clinical SLAs—if the triage p99 is missed we have to divert traffic. So we need an automatic fallback in place. Do you have fallback policies?
[03:24] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports routing fallbacks: model variant fallback, region fallback, and degraded-mode responses. We can set up canary -> primary routing with automatic rollback on error rate or latency regressions.
[03:36] Jorge (contractor): Sorry jumped in, how does KV cache behave with canaries? If we route 5% traffic to canary, will cache cold starts affect latency metrics unfairly?
[03:47] Ethan: Good question. We recommend a warm-up plan—pre-fill cache, or steady ramp for canaries. Our runtime exposes KV cache metrics and we can pin cache warmers in the runbook. We'll include a pre-warm step in the pilot playbook.
[04:03] Samir: On connectivity: do you need inbound open ports? Our security team doesn't want public IPs talking to internal services.
[04:11] Sophie: For Private/VPC we don't require opening inbound to your infra; we deploy inside your VPC or use PrivateLink endpoints. Hosted with PrivateLink is the path if you don't want a full Private deployment.
[04:24] Laura: We'll need the exact network CIDR ranges and ports to review with our firewall team.
[04:29] Maya: We'll share a one-pager with the CIDRs, port list, and expected egress patterns.
[04:35] [05:00] (short pause as people look at a deck link posted in chat)
[05:05] Ethan: I put a link in chat to the pilot checklist and the Dedicated sizing spreadsheet. The spreadsheet has throughput estimates for common models and guidance on quantization/instance mix.
[05:16] Dr. Anna: Good, our summarizer uses 4K context and is GPT-family derived, triage is 1K context. Do you have quantized variants supported?
[05:26] Ethan: Yes, the runtime supports INT8/4 quantizations and we've verified fidelity for common summarization workloads. For clinical text we recommend running a small eval to check quality drift before rolling a quantized variant. Redwood Optimize can run automated eval sets and regression alerts.
[05:41] Tom: What about model versioning and pinning? We need to make sure future fine-tuned versions don't silently break prod.
[05:49] Sophie: You can pin model version per route, and we support canary A/B rollouts and automatic rollback on regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
[05:58] Laura: On auditability: can we export raw request/response payloads (PII redacted) to our SIEM?
[06:06] Ethan: Audit logs include request metadata and token-level cost. We can also set up webhook sinks for payload copies to your S3 if you want; we'll need to align on PII redaction rules.
[06:18] Dr. Anna: For evaluation, we need a way to run golden prompts against each model and compare outputs. Is that supported?
[06:25] Sophie: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports eval suites and will trigger alerts if quality deviates beyond configured thresholds. We'll demo that in the next call.
[06:33] Samir: Ops questions—what visibility do we get into per-model latency by host, token breakdown, and per-request trace IDs?
[06:41] Ethan: Console exposes token-level latency, host-level breakdowns, per-route traces, and a tracing hook you can pipe to your tracing backend. We also surface autoscaler events and batch sizes used over time.
[06:53] [07:00] Dr. Anna: Budget question—if we start Hosted and then move to Dedicated, how do the costs compare? Any contractual commitment for Dedicated?
[07:09] Maya: Dedicated is a reserved capacity product with monthly commitments, and it's priced for predictable throughput. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with higher per-token cost but less commitment. We can run a cost model comparing your expected QPS and token lengths; Ethan will prepare a comparison.
[07:23] Ethan: I'll model two scenarios: Hosted steady + burst vs Dedicated small pool with autoscaling burst; will include sensitivity for quantization and batching.
[07:32] Tom: Regarding release controls, can we set environment-based routing? e.g., dev -> staging -> prod?
[07:38] Sophie: Yes, we support per-environment routing and role-based access to prevent prod keys leaking into staging.
[07:44] Laura: For SSO—SAML is fine. We also require SCIM for provisioning and want to tie audit logs to Okta user IDs. Is SCIM supported?
[07:53] Maya: Yes, SCIM provisioning is supported for enterprise accounts. We'll include SCIM docs in the security pack.
[07:59] [08:05] Samir: Are there any pre-approved cloud partners for Private deployments? We prefer to avoid redesigning our infra.
[08:12] Ethan: Private deployments can be run in your AWS account or in our managed private control plane with connectors. For on-prem, we have an appliance option but that's less common.
[08:21] Dr. Anna: Timelines—what would a minimal pilot look like? We want to be live for triage in ~6 weeks. Is that realistic?
[08:29] Maya: 6 weeks is aggressive but doable if we have a clear path: security sign-off, network connectivity, and sample traffic. Week 1: security & network, week 2-3: integration + small pilot, week 4: performance tuning, week 5-6: canary + rollback and go-live.
[08:44] Jorge: I can help provide traffic patterns and replay logs for week 2.
[08:48] Ethan: Excellent—send sample request logs and we'll craft a benchmark. We'll also include a runbook for cache warmup, batch sizing, and monitoring thresholds.
[08:58] [09:10] (Laura types in chat: "What about data residency for EU patients?")
[09:16] Laura: We do have EU patients; we need data residency controls too.
[09:21] Maya: We support region-restricted deployments. We can either pin model serving to eu-west-1 or use a Private deployment in your EU account. We'll document options.
[09:32] Dr. Anna: One more ML question—how does Redwood handle KV cache invalidation if we update a model quickly? We can't serve stale cached embeddings.
[09:41] Ethan: Cache keys are tied to model version; when you pin a new model version we can either invalidate cache or keep caches isolated per variant to avoid cross-bleed. We'll recommend per-variant cache namespaces for safe rollouts.
[09:56] Tom: What's the escalation path if a regression hits in prod during clinic hours?
[10:01] Sophie: We'll set up alerting thresholds and a pager rotation for on-call SEs; plus automatic rollback triggers on error-rate or latency SLO breach. We'll also create a post-incident runbook.
[10:12] Maya: Quick recap of immediate deliverables: Maya/Ethan will send security pack + network CIDRs + Dedicated sizing spreadsheet by 2025-08-04. Ethan will propose pilot benchmark plan and runbook by 2025-08-11. Solstice will share traffic logs and PII classification by 2025-08-07. Does that sound right?
[10:28] Dr. Anna: Yes. Also can we set the next meeting to be infrastructure/runbook deep-dive with our infra and security?
[10:35] Maya: Absolutely—how about week of Aug 11th, Ethan lead?
[10:39] Samir: Works for me.
[10:42] Laura: Works for security as long as we have the docs first.
[10:45] [11:00] (everyone agrees on calendar)
[11:05] Ethan: One more note: we'll include a small checklist for regulatory review—what to expect for SOC2 + artifact collection. It helps speed the legal review.
[11:14] Dr. Anna: Perfect. Also any recommended Eval prompt sets for clinical summarization we can reuse?
[11:20] Sophie: We'll share a sample eval pack used by other health customers (anonymized).
[11:26] Tom: For the pilot, prefer no model fine-tuning until after initial stability tests.
[11:30] Maya: Noted.
[11:33] [12:00] (chat link: "security-pack-redwood.pdf")
[12:04] Laura: I'll review the pack and send any gaps.
[12:08] Maya: Thanks all. Final recap and next steps we captured in chat; we'll follow up with calendar invite for the infra deep dive and attach the security pack.
[12:18] Dr. Anna: Great, thank you.
[12:21] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email. Bye.

End of transcript.
